name: s2
title: Call of Duty: WWII (S2)
note: Addresses from the decrypted s2_mp64_ship.exe (same TimeDateStamp 0x6963a4d9 and section layout as the installed exe), rebased to its runtime base and flattened so file offset == RVA. Primitives found 2026-09-25 by disassembly, starting from Load_Stream (the most called function whose callers store a var global and pass a size).

ghidra.epilogue_tags_note: the stream stack depth the inlined pop tail decrements

transcriber_note: tables from the readers' machine code (the machine-code transcriber): the readers take their struct from var globals, the shape the C transcriber does not read
rva_note: file_read(dst, n) copies zone bytes. Load_Stream(flag, dst, n): block 2 memsets, block 3 does nothing, any other block reads. No string primitive: Load_XString (load_string) and the script-string reader (load_string_ptr: reads the text, then SL_GetString) call file_read one byte at a time, which stream.byte_strings folds into one string read. resolve: *p = base[p>>32] + (u32)p - 1; resolve_deref the same, dereferenced. alloc: align the stream to 8 (only the asset list uses the call; readers inline it).

asset_dispatch.note: the game's asset loop (DB_LoadXFile tail, 0x4a61fc): varXAsset = &list[i]; Load_XAsset(false). Load_XAsset reads nothing (flag 0) and hands &header to Load_XAssetHeader (0x4c57e0), an if-chain over the type calling each Load_<T>Ptr.

stream.growing_note: every block but the dead ones (2 memsets, 3 reads nothing) and 6, which pop (0x4d6a30) rewinds; reads land in 0, 6 and rarely 4

stream_note: a back reference is block << 32 | offset + 1 (resolve 0x4d6b70), so every 64-bit value is a pointer the loader could have written (backref_max_nibble 0xf): the readers' own tests (== -1, > -3, != 0) decide. insert_ptr (0x4d6920) reserves the resident slot in block 0.

release.note: thresholds the release check enforces before these tables ship

zone_load.note: the tail of DB_LoadXFile (0x4a6154): the 0x28-byte XAssetList is raw-read into the caller's buffer, then under push(0) the script strings and XGlobals load through their own readers, then under push(0) the asset array is allocated, Load_Stream-ed, and each entry dispatched with varXAsset = &list[i]; Load_XAsset(false). The zone's XFile header is in the container, so the list is at offset 0.
zone_load.add_asset_note: DB_AddXAsset (0xa4390) and its per-type wrappers (rcx = &header slot, the type in ecx at the inner call): the game copies the struct, loaded into the temporary block 6, into its pool and points the slot at the copy. The zone format does the same.

crt_note: IAT thunks (jmp [rip+x]) the emulator performs itself: names from the shipped exe's import table.
